s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Ulcer has a clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes and giant cells
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Oral histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo found in histiocytes and giant cells, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Oral cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intracellular yeasts and granulomatous inflammation, although less common than histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Oral tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic oral ulceration, with tuberculosis being a common cause in endemic regions

shortlist.label: Oral blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and histopathological features to histoplasmosis, although less common in this region

shortlist.label: Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammation and granulomatous reaction, although less likely given the presence of intracellular yeasts

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo in histiocytes and giant cells, as seen in the histopathological examination, is characteristic of histoplasmosis. The patient's residence in eastern India, a region with possible exposure to Histoplasma capsulatum, and the clinical presentation of a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oral cryptococcosis
rejected.why: While cryptococcosis can present with similar histopathological features, the lack of encapsulated yeast forms and the negative HIV serology make it less likely.

rejected.label: Oral tuberculosis
rejected.why: The absence of caseating granulomas and the presence of intracellular yeasts are not typical of tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Oral blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with broad-based budding yeast forms, which were not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Chronic sclerosing sialadenitis
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the salivary glands and does not typically present with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue.
